question_text: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by the body’s response to an infection. These infections are typically bacterial but may be fungal, parasitic, or viral. The body’s response to these infections leads to increased inflammation and organ damage. This damage, in turn, results in a weakened immune system, which increases the likelihood of reinfection. In a recent study, a team of doctors and pharmacologists led by Shubham Soni claims that administering ketone esters can reduce inflammation and immune system weakening caused by sepsis. Which finding from the team led by Soni, if true, would most directly support its claim?
options: Patients with sepsis who were administered ketone esters had fewer signs of inflammation and less organ damage than those administered standard antibiotics.
When administered, ketone esters are known to increase blood ketone levels, which in turn are a source of energy for the brain.
Both those patients administered ketone esters and those administered standard antibiotics did not have reduced inflammation when treated with medication intended to reduce fever.

Those sepsis patients administered ketone esters had reduced inflammation but greater organ damage than those administered standard antibiotics.
